q-107608.name: Question 1
q-107608.problem: What is the volume of a rectangular solid that has length, width, and height of $9\,\text{ft},$ $4\,\text{ft},$ and $5\,\text{ft},$ respectively?
q-107608.worked_solution:
We can find the volume $V$ of the rectangular prism using the formula

$$
V=lwh,
$$

where $l$ is the length, $w$ is the width, and $h$ is the height of the solid.

Substituting 

$$
l=9\,\text{ft},\,w=4\,\text{ft},\,h=5\,\text{ft}
$$

into the formula, we obtain

$$
V=9\cdot 4\cdot 5=180\,{\text{ft}}^{3}.
$$

$$
V=lwh,

q-118851.name: Question 6
q-118851.problem: The height of a rectangular solid is $2\sqrt{3}\,\text{m}$ and its volume is $24\sqrt{3}\,{\text{m}}^{3}.$ If the base  (length × width) of the solid is a square, find the length of the solid.
q-118851.worked_solution:
We can find the volume $V$ of the rectangular prism using the formula

$$
V=lwh,
$$

where $l$ is the length, $w$ is the width, and $h$ is the height of the solid.

Since the base of the rectangular solid is a square, we have that 

$$
l=w.
$$

Substituting 

$$
V=24\sqrt{3},\,h=2\sqrt{3},\,w=l
$$

into the formula, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =lwh \\ V & ={l}^{2}h \\ 24\sqrt{3} & ={l}^{2}\cdot 2\sqrt{3} \\ {l}^{2} & =12 \\ l & =2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the length is $2\sqrt{3}\,\text{m}.$

V=lwh,

where l is the length, w is the width, and h is the height of the solid.

Substituting

l=35cm,w=35cm,h=28cm

into the formula, we obtain

V=35⋅35⋅28=34300cm3.

Finally, to fill the tank to capacity, it would cost

34300⋅0.0016=$54.88.
